messages:
maria: quick heads-up — discovered a UX hole in the Go SDK generator: ctx cancel doesn't always stop streaming if auth refresh kicks in.
kevin: oof, that's confusing. do you have a tiny repro?
maria: yep, minimal:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 1*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, _ := client.Generate(ctx, req)
for resp.Next() { fmt.Println(resp.Token()) }
```
if auth refresh happens during the stream, we still see tokens after cancel.
oliver: sounds like the refresh runs with background context and the retry spawns a goroutine that isn't tied to the original ctx.
sara: can repro locally. logs show: "auth: refresh start" -> "ctx canceled" -> "auth: refresh done" -> more tokens.
kevin: that's a bug. we intentionally used background for refresh to avoid leaking, but for streams we need cooperative cancel.
maria: worked around by calling resp.Close() in sample app cleanup, but users expect ctx cancel to be sufficient.
kevin: plan: make auth refresh accept parent ctx, bail if parent done, and audit retry goroutine lifetimes. add a test simulating immediate cancel mid-stream.
oliver: also check buffered token channel sizes — backpressure matters. if we buffer too much, cancel won't prevent queued tokens from being delivered.
sara: filed issue #4312 for triage.
dev-bot: created issue #4312: "go-sdk: generator stream continues after context cancel when auth refresh in-flight" assigned to @kevin.
kevin: putting up a WIP PR touching client/transport/retry.go and auth/refresh.go. will add changelog & patch release if canary is green.
maria: happy to validate sample apps and update README with a short note until patch lands. thanks!
